slides.title: One firm and one matter
body: Kampala Legal and Tax acts for Victoria Services Ltd, the customer. Equator Systems Ltd, its service provider, proposes an internal group reorganisation. Victoria asks whether consent is required. A related team reviews Victoria’s September 2026 records. The firms, companies and client records are fictional.
The same agreement, records and source register will return throughout the course.
slides.explain: Introduce the people and the commercial question before any terminology. The provider Equator proposes an internal group reorganisation and asks what its service agreement requires. The tax team also needs to reconcile September records.

slides.title: AI systems
body: An AI system infers from inputs how to produce predictions, content, recommendations or decisions for explicit or implicit objectives. Systems vary in autonomy and adaptation.
AI is also the field concerned with building and studying such systems.
slides.explain: This is a paraphrase of the OECD AI-system definition, not a quotation defining the entire academic field. Inference distinguishes deriving an output from merely storing a record. It does not establish accuracy or autonomy in every product.
slides.question: Does the definition tell us that a particular product is reliable?
slides.answer: No. A field definition does not establish task performance.

slides.title: Two phases of a retrieval system
slides.explain: Walk through two separate paths. During preparation an embedding model converts chunks into vectors stored with metadata in an index. At question time an embedding model represents the query; retrieval and optional keyword matching select permitted current passages. A language model then generates an answer using those passages and instructions. These are distinct roles; implementations can combine services and retrieval need not always be vector-based.

slides.title: Direct context, RAG and CAG
slides.explain: Teach context limits and answer relevance rather than insisting on a vector database for every task. Context caching can reuse supported computation; it does not update stale evidence by itself. CAG is a specialised context-caching approach, not a synonym for all caching. Cache-augmented generation (CAG) preloads a manageable collection and reuses supported cached computation; it is not parameter training or guaranteed permanent memory. Corpus size, access and updates still matter.
slides.question: When might direct context be sufficient?
slides.answer: A manageable, permitted set of documents for a bounded question.

right: Use retrieval with source, access and update controls.
